info.title: Dataverse Synapse Link Orchestration API (athena)
info.description:
The Synapse Link orchestration service (internally *athena*) drives Dataverse's Link to Microsoft Fabric and Azure Synapse: choosing which tables to mirror, creating the Fabric lakehouse artifacts, and managing the resulting lake profile.

The host is per environment, derived from the environment's cluster suffix and the compass direction of its Azure region.

Changing a link's table list is a three-call sequence — update the lake profile, activate it, then refresh the lakehouse artifacts — and per-table sync progress is reported on the profile.

Unofficial and reverse-engineered — see the [README](https://github.com/AdamCoulterOz/powerplatform-apis/tree/main/athena) for how it was derived and which parts are verified.
info.x-source: Rewritten from 18 browser HAR captures (291 recorded calls) of make.powerapps.com and app.fabric.microsoft.com driving real Link to Fabric workflows on a live tenant, plus live directory and DNS probing of the host and the service principal. Supersedes the earlier revision, which was derived from an unmerged Terraform provider feature branch and covered 3 of the 15 operations.

servers.description:
Per-environment host, composed rather than published: no environment or tenant endpoint advertises it. Read the environment from BAPI (GET /providers/Microsoft.BusinessAppPlatform/scopes/admin/environments/{environmentId}) and join two of its fields -- properties.cluster.uriSuffix supplies clusterUriSuffix, and the compass-direction prefix of properties.azureRegion supplies azureRegionPrefix. The two concatenate with no separator, which is why the result reads as though a stray letter had been prepended to the cluster suffix.

Worked example: an environment reporting cluster.uriSuffix us-il102.gateway.prod.island and azureRegion eastus resolves to athenawebservice.eus-il102.gateway.prod.island.powerapps.com.

**The prefix is not a constant.** One island scale unit is reached under a different hostname from each Azure region it serves -- e{island} for environments in australiaeast and se{island} for environments in australiasoutheast, with identical cluster.uriSuffix values. The prefix varies with the environment's Azure region while the cluster suffix stays put, and a client that hardcodes one prefix will send australiasoutheast environments to a hostname that does not exist.

DNS cannot be used to check a composed host: *.{azureRegionPrefix}{clusterUriSuffix}.powerapps.com is a wildcard onto the island's ingress gateway, so arbitrary hostnames resolve. The gateway routes on the Host header, and only the response distinguishes a real service from an invented one -- a registered upstream answers with x-ms-webservice, x-servicefabric and an upstream server-timing entry, while an unregistered hostname on the same island is rejected by the gateway itself with a bare 404 carrying none of those headers.

azureRegionPrefix.description:
The compass-direction component of the environment's Azure region, lowercased, with the geography dropped: australiaeast and eastus both give e, australiasoutheast gives se, westus and westeurope give w, northeurope gives n. The geography itself is already carried by clusterUriSuffix, so this prefix supplies only the direction.

A wrong prefix does not produce a helpful error -- it produces NXDOMAIN.
azureRegionPrefix.x-observed-values-note: e and se were observed in recorded traffic against the same island scale unit, from environments in australiaeast and australiasoutheast respectively. n and w were confirmed by DNS against real island scale units. The set is plainly larger than these four -- every Azure region hosting a Power Platform island contributes one -- so no enum is asserted.

clusterUriSuffix.description: The environment's gateway cluster, taken verbatim from properties.cluster.uriSuffix on the BAPI environment. It names the island scale unit that serves the environment and is stable for the life of the environment. Every BAPI api-version from 2020-10-01 onward returns it. Two environments in different Azure regions of the same geography share a cluster suffix and differ only in azureRegionPrefix.

tags.name: Linkable Tables
tags.description: The catalogue of tables and relationships in a Dataverse organization that a Fabric or Synapse link may include, together with the reason any of them cannot be included. This is what the wizard's table picker is built from. It is organization-scoped rather than environment-scoped -- every operation on it is addressed by organizationUrl rather than by a path id -- and it is read-only: enabling a table for linking is done by adding it to a lake profile, not here.

tags.name: Fabric Workspaces
tags.description: The Microsoft Fabric workspaces that the calling user may target with a mirror lakehouse, as athena sees them. athena proxies this from Fabric rather than requiring the caller to hold a Fabric token, which is the only reason it exists on this surface; the authoritative list is Fabric's own. Choosing one of these supplies the WorkspaceId for lakehouse artifact creation.

tags.name: Lakehouse Artifacts
tags.description:
The set of Fabric artifacts that back one environment's Link to Fabric: a mirror lakehouse created inside a caller-supplied Fabric workspace, the SQL analytics endpoint over it, and the binding to the Fabric-to-Dataverse connection that keeps it fed. Creating them also writes the Dataverse-side rows -- the synapselinkprofile and its datalakefolder -- which the caller never creates directly.

There is no read and no list on this resource; its state is observed through the Data Lakes and Lake Profiles resources instead. Creation is not idempotent in the usual sense: re-posting to it with an existing lake's ids is how the link's shortcut set is resynchronised after the table list changes.

tags.name: Data Lakes
tags.description:
The data lake destinations attached to an environment -- one row per Dataverse datalakefolder. For a Link to Fabric the row describes the managed lakehouse athena provisioned (IsManaged true, with LakehouseId and LakehouseWorkspaceId populated); for a bring-your-own Azure Data Lake Storage link it describes the customer's storage account instead. An environment with no link has none.

This is the resource that makes the link observable. Its Id is the datalakefolder id, which is both the path id for the Lake Profiles resource and the id required to delete the lakehouse artifacts.

tags.name: Lake Profiles
tags.description:
The synapselinkprofile behind one data lake: which Dataverse tables are being mirrored, how each is partitioned and batched, and how far each has got through initial sync and delta sync. It is created as a side effect of creating lakehouse artifacts and destroyed with them; the operations here read it, replace it, and restart its jobs.

Addressed by the datalakefolder id, not by the profile's own Id. The profile carries its own Id in the body and it is a different GUID -- passing it in the path will not find the profile.

tags.name: Organization Registration
tags.description: The Dataverse organization's record with the athena island that serves it, and the preflight checks a client runs before offering to link. An organization that has never been linked is unknown to its island, and environment-scoped calls for it fail until the record is written. Registration is a one-time bootstrap per organization rather than a resource with a lifecycle: there is no read, no delete, and re-writing it is harmless -- the portals rewrite it on almost every visit.

get.description:
Every table in the organization that a link could include, with the ones that cannot be included flagged rather than omitted.

The response is large -- a modestly customised environment returns between 700 and 730 rows -- and it is neither paged nor filterable: there is no paging, no $top and no ordering parameter. Rows come back sorted by DisplayName.

Organization-scoped: it takes no environment id, only organizationUrl, so a caller that has resolved the host for one environment can read the catalogue of any organization served by the same island.

200.description: The organization's tables. Never empty in practice -- a Dataverse organization always has system tables.

get.description:
The organization's many-to-many relationships, so a caller can offer their intersect tables for mirroring. Mirroring both ends of an N:N relationship does not carry the join across; the intersect table named here has to be linked as a table in its own right.

Unpaged and unfiltered, like the table list. Only relationships whose IsIntersect is true are returned -- one-to-many relationships do not appear here.

The Dynamics 365 Finance and Operations tables available to the organization, for an environment whose Dataverse organization is linked to an F&O environment. Both portals call it unconditionally alongside the Dataverse table list.

An organization with no F&O link gets an empty array.

parameters.name: retrieveComoSelectedFnOTables
parameters.description: Return only the tables already selected under the organization's COMO configuration, rather than all available ones. The portals send false.

200.description: The available Finance and Operations tables; empty for an organization with no F&O link.

get.description:
Whether COMO is enabled for the organization. COMO is the capability behind the Finance and Operations table selection -- it is what IsComoTableActive on a Dataverse table and retrieveComoSelectedFnOTables on the Finance and Operations table list both refer to -- and its expansion is not documented publicly. The portals call this while preparing an unlink, to decide whether F&O-side state also has to be considered.

Organization-scoped: no environment id, only organizationUrl.

200.description: A bare JSON boolean: true when COMO is enabled for the organization.

get.description:
Whether the island scale unit serving this environment has athena enabled for the organization. Both portals call it first when opening the link management page, as the gate on showing anything else.

It answers false rather than failing for an organization the island does not know, which makes it the cheapest safe check of whether the derived host is the right one for an environment -- unlike every other operation here, calling it changes nothing.

200.description: A bare JSON boolean: true when the island serving the environment has athena enabled for the organization, false when the island does not know it.

get.description:
The client credential the environment's encryption enterprise policy exposes to the sync engine, for a customer-managed-key environment. "ep" in the path is the enterprise policy. The portals call it immediately before writing the organization registration, so that a CMK environment's link is configured with the right identity to reach the customer's key.

An environment with no enterprise policy gets nulls rather than an error.

200.description: The credential, or a pair of nulls when no enterprise policy applies. Served as text/plain despite the body being JSON -- a client that dispatches on Content-Type will not parse it.

post.description:
Register the Dataverse organization with the athena island serving its environment, or refresh the registration if it is already there.

**The organization details are query parameters, not a body.** Send no body: the request carries Content-Length: 0, and anything sent as a body is ignored.

Idempotent and cheap. The portals call it on almost every visit to the link management page rather than tracking whether it has been done, and again immediately before creating or resynchronising lakehouse artifacts.

Its role in the wizard's error handling is the part worth copying: an unregistered organization does not fail at link creation, it fails earlier and more obscurely, on the premium-licence check. See that operation's 403 for the sequence.

200.description: The organization is registered. The response body is empty, served as text/plain; there is nothing to read from it.

get.description:
The Fabric workspaces the calling user can target, proxied from Fabric by athena so that the caller needs only an athena token. Unpaged, and returned in no documented order.

The list reflects the *user's* Fabric access, not the environment's: the same user gets the same list from environments on different islands, and a workspace created in Fabric shows up on the next call. Filter to workspaces with a capacityId before offering them, since a workspace with no Fabric capacity cannot host a mirror lakehouse.

200.description: The workspaces available to the caller.

get.description:
The data lake destinations attached to the environment. **This is how a caller discovers whether an environment is linked at all**, and it is the only operation that yields the datalakefolder id that every other environment-scoped operation is addressed by.

An empty array means no link. After an unlink it goes empty about thirty seconds after the delete returns, which makes it the natural way to confirm the unlink completed.

Reading Dataverse directly is not a substitute: the cds2_workspace and cds3_workspace rows exist in the datalakefolders table on every organization whether or not it has ever been linked, so matching on unique name there cannot distinguish a linked environment from an unlinked one. This operation returns only rows that back a real link.

parameters.name: fetchLakehouseInfo
parameters.description: Populate LakehouseId and LakehouseWorkspaceId by querying Fabric. Send true whenever the Fabric-side ids are needed.

parameters.name: isManagedLake
parameters.description: Restrict the result to athena-managed lakes (a Link to Fabric) rather than customer-supplied storage. Sent only alongside isCDS3, and omitted entirely on the calls that just test whether a link exists.

parameters.name: isCDS3
parameters.description: Restrict the result to the cds3_workspace folder, excluding the older cds2_workspace Synapse Link folder. Note that this filters correctly even though the IsCDS3 field on the returned rows is false.

200.description: The environment's lakes; an empty array when the environment has no link.

post.description:
Provision the environment's Link to Fabric, or resynchronise an existing one. Two request shapes share the route and are told apart by the query string as much as by the body.

**Create** (no adlsShortcuts, no removeShortcutsFirst) creates a mirror lakehouse in the named Fabric workspace, binds it to the named Fabric-to-Dataverse connection, writes the synapselinkprofile and datalakefolder rows into Dataverse, and starts initial sync of the named tables. It is synchronous, returning 200 with the artifact ids after roughly forty seconds. Initial sync is not -- poll the lake profile for that.

**Resynchronise** (removeShortcutsFirst=true) targets a lake that already exists, by LakeId and FolderId, and rebuilds its Fabric shortcuts to match the profile's current table list. It carries no table list of its own; the tables are changed first through the lake profile, and this call makes Fabric agree. It returns in about a second.

Register the organization first. Both portals call the organization registration update immediately before this on every run, including runs where the organization was plainly already registered.

**The response is plain JSON**: an object served with Content-Type: application/json.

parameters.name: removeShortcutsFirst
parameters.description: Delete the lakehouse's existing Fabric shortcuts before recreating them, so that tables removed from the profile stop appearing in Fabric. Sent as true only with the resynchronise body shape.

parameters.name: adlsShortcuts
parameters.description: Create the shortcuts against the customer's own Azure Data Lake Storage rather than the managed lake. False for a Link to Fabric.

requestBody.description: The create shape when establishing a link, the resynchronise shape when rebuilding one. Send every field of whichever shape applies.

200.description: The link exists and the artifacts are named. Returned by both shapes, and by a resynchronise that changed nothing.

get.description:
Whether the tenant has the Power BI premium or Fabric capacity entitlement that a mirror lakehouse requires. Both portals call it as the gate on offering to link at all.

It is also, unexpectedly, the operation that surfaces an unregistered organization -- see its 403. That makes it the one call worth making first on an environment whose registration state is unknown.

200.description: A bare JSON boolean: true when the tenant has the entitlement.

403.description:
The organization is not registered with this island. The body is empty -- Content-Length: 0, no Content-Type, no error code -- so the status is the whole signal, and it is indistinguishable at the transport level from a genuine authorization failure.

The fix is to register the organization and retry, and that is exactly what both portals do: this 403 is followed within 200 milliseconds by an organization registration update and then by a repeat of this call, which returns 200. Do not treat it as fatal on first sight, and do not register speculatively either -- the portals wait to be told.

delete.description:
Unlink the environment: remove the Fabric shortcuts and lakehouse athena provisioned, and delete the synapselinkprofile and datalakefolder rows from Dataverse.

Get the path id from the Data Lakes list, whose Id field is exactly this value. Do not pick it out of the Dataverse datalakefolders table instead: a stock organization carries about ten datalakefolder rows, including msdyn_analytics and msdyn_processadvisor, and the cds3_workspace and cds2_workspace rows are present whether or not the environment has ever been linked. The Data Lakes list returns only rows that back a real link.

Synchronous but not instant: it returns 200 after roughly ten seconds, and the Data Lakes list goes empty about thirty seconds later.

200.description: The link is gone. The response body is empty, served as text/plain. Confirm by re-reading the Data Lakes list rather than by trusting the status alone.

get.description:
The profile behind one lake, with per-table sync state. **This is the progress endpoint**: after creating lakehouse artifacts, poll it until every entry's CurrentState reaches InProgress, which means that table's initial sync and post-processing are done and it is queryable in Fabric. Do not poll the profile-level Status.InitialSyncState instead -- it reads Completed while the profile's tables are still mid-sync.

The path id is the datalakefolder id, not the profile's own Id.

parameters.name: status
parameters.description: Include the per-table Status block and the profile-level Status. Send true to get the sync counters.

parameters.name: publishErrorMessageToUI
parameters.description: Populate ErrorDetails.Message with text intended for display rather than leaving it to be resolved from the code. The portals send true.

parameters.name: isManagedLake
parameters.description: Assert that the target is an athena-managed lake rather than customer-supplied storage. It makes no difference to the response for a managed lake; the portals send it on some reads of a profile and omit it on others.

put.description:
Replace the profile: change which tables are mirrored and how each is partitioned and batched. **This is how tables are added to and removed from an existing link** -- there is no add-table or remove-table operation, and re-posting lakehouse artifacts does not change the table list.

It is a whole-document replace, not a merge. Read the profile, edit it, and send the whole thing back, with Entities reduced from the fifty-odd fields per table that the read returns to the six the update accepts. A table omitted from Entities is removed from the link.

It does not take effect on its own. Follow it within a few seconds with an activate on the same profile, and then -- where the table list changed -- with a lakehouse-artifacts resynchronise, so that Fabric's shortcuts match the new list. All three steps are needed; the update alone leaves the profile changed and the sync jobs still running the old list.

requestBody.description: The complete desired profile: every field read back from the profile, with the changes applied.

200.description: The profile was replaced. Only its id and state come back; re-read the profile to see the stored result, including the defaults the service filled in.

post.description:
Apply the profile: restart the sync jobs against the profile's current table list, and set ActivationTime. Send no body -- the request carries Content-Length: 0.

Always paired with an update, a few seconds after it. An update that is never activated leaves the stored profile changed and the running sync unchanged. The call returns immediately; the work it starts is visible only through the profile's per-table CurrentState, where a newly added table appears at InitialSyncNotStarted.

200.description: The profile was activated. Returns its id and state, identically to update.

azure_auth.description:
Microsoft Entra ID OAuth2 against the first-party application "Azure Synapse Link for Dataverse" (7f15f9d9-cad0-44f1-bbba-d36650e07765), owned by the Microsoft first-party tenant. The audience is that application, not the PowerApps service, and the generic Power Platform scopes are not accepted -- a client that guesses the scope from the hostname will guess service.powerapps.com and be wrong.

The service accepts a token whose aud claim is the bare application id 7f15f9d9-cad0-44f1-bbba-d36650e07765, so the GUID form of the scope is the form to request. The identifier-URI form (https://exporttodatalake.com/.default) is issuable but produces a different aud claim.

The application publishes exactly one delegated permission, user_impersonation, whose admin-consent text reads "Have access to Dynamics 365 Athena - CDS to Azure data lake API" -- the surviving trace of the service's internal name and of its origin as Export to Data Lake. It publishes **no application roles at all**, so an app-only client-credentials token carries no roles claim and cannot be authorized for anything here. A delegated user token is required: accepted tokens carry scp: user_impersonation and idtyp: user.

Nothing on this host issues a WWW-Authenticate challenge. An unauthenticated call, a wrong-audience token and a syntactically invalid bearer token all produce the same bodiless 404 as an unrouted path, because routing fails before authentication runs. The audience cannot be discovered from the service; it is only knowable from the token.

scopes.7f15f9d9-cad0-44f1-bbba-d36650e07765/.de: Azure Synapse Link for Dataverse (athena). The form observed in every recorded request, and the form the Terraform provider uses.
scopes.https://exporttodatalake.com/.default: The same application addressed by its identifier URI. Issuable, and a useful reminder of what the service is, but never observed against the service.

environmentId.name: environmentId
environmentId.description: The Power Platform environment id, as BAPI reports it in the environment's name field. Note that this is not the Dataverse organization id -- the two are different GUIDs for the same environment, and several operations here take both.

tenantId.name: tenantId
tenantId.description: The Entra tenant that owns the environment.

datalakeFolderId.name: datalakeFolderId
datalakeFolderId.description: The Dataverse datalakefolder id that identifies the lake to unlink. Read it from the Id field of the Data Lakes list for this environment; do not confuse it with LakehouseId, which names the Fabric lakehouse and is a different GUID in the same payload.

profileId.name: profileId
profileId.description: The **datalakefolder id**, despite the path segment being named lakeprofile. It is the Id field of the Data Lakes list, and it is the same value the delete operation takes as datalakeFolderId. The profile's own Id, returned in the response body, is a different GUID and is not accepted here.

organizationUrlQuery.name: organizationUrl
organizationUrlQuery.description: The Dataverse organization's instance URL, with its trailing slash. The service accepts it percent-encoded or raw.

organizationIdQuery.name: organizationId
organizationIdQuery.description: The Dataverse organization id -- the organizationid column, not the environment id.

dxt.name: dxt
dxt.description: Selects the Dataverse Export Toolkit variant of the operation. Pass false for the standard behaviour.

xMsOrganizationId.name: x-ms-organization-id
xMsOrganizationId.description: The Dataverse organization id. Environment-scoped operations use it to resolve the organization context; without it the service cannot tell which organization inside the environment the call is about.

xMsOrganizationIdOptional.name: x-ms-organization-id
xMsOrganizationIdOptional.description: The Dataverse organization id. The operations that carry organizationUrl in the query resolve the organization from that and succeed without this header; send it on the rest.

xMsCorrelationId.name: x-ms-correlation-id
xMsCorrelationId.description: Client-generated correlation id. Echoed back on the response, and the value the service logs against the request -- worth setting and keeping a note of if you will ever need Microsoft to trace a failure.

xMsClientRequestId.name: x-ms-client-request-id
xMsClientRequestId.description: Client-generated per-request id. The Fabric portal sends this where the maker portal sends x-ms-correlation-id; both are accepted everywhere.

DataverseTable.description: One Dataverse table as a link candidate: its identity, whether it can be included in a link at all, and why not if it cannot.

LogicalName.description: The table's logical name. This is the value to put in Entities and EntityDescriptions[].Type when creating or updating a link.

IsActivity.description: Whether the table is an activity table. Activity tables are linkable, but they mirror the activitypointer base table's columns alongside their own.

IsDisabled.description: Whether the table cannot currently be added to a link. The wizard greys these out rather than hiding them, so that ReasonIfDisabled can be shown.

ReasonIfDisabled.description: Why the table cannot be linked, as display text; empty string when IsDisabled is false. The common value is "Change Tracking is Disabled" -- enabling change tracking on the table in Dataverse is what clears it. Other reasons exist, such as long-term retention and elastic tables, so treat the field as free text rather than an enumeration.

IsComoTableActive.description: Whether the table is already selected under the organization's COMO configuration. COMO is the Finance and Operations-linked table selection this service also serves through the Finance and Operations table list; its expansion is not documented publicly. False throughout an organization with no F&O link.

IsVirtualEntity.description: Whether the table is a virtual table backed by an external data source. Virtual tables appear in the catalogue rather than being filtered out.

Description.description: The table's Dataverse description, which is frequently empty.

FinanceAndOperationsTable.description: One Dynamics 365 Finance and Operations table as a link candidate, returned only for an environment whose Dataverse organization is linked to an F&O environment.

EntityRelationship.description: One many-to-many relationship between two Dataverse tables. The wizard uses these to offer the intersect tables that carry an N:N relationship, which must be mirrored explicitly if the relationship is to be reconstructable in the lake -- linking both ends of an N:N does not bring the join with it.

Name.description: Display key for the relationship, formed as the two table logical names joined by a hyphen. Not unique: two relationships between the same pair of tables share it, and are told apart by SchemaName.

IsIntersect.description: Whether the relationship is carried by an intersect table. True on every row this operation returns, which lists only N:N relationships.

IntersectLogicalName.description: Logical name of the intersect table that stores the relationship's rows. This is the value to add to a link's table list to mirror the relationship.

SchemaName.description: The relationship's schema name, which is unique where Name is not.

FabricWorkspace.description: A Microsoft Fabric workspace the caller may create a mirror lakehouse in. Note the camelCase field names: this is the only payload on the surface that is not PascalCase, because athena passes Fabric's own representation through.

id.description: The Fabric workspace id. This is the WorkspaceId to send when creating lakehouse artifacts.

name.description: The workspace's display name, for presenting the choice to a user.

capacityId.description: The Fabric capacity backing the workspace. It comes back as an upper-case GUID while every other id on this surface is lower-case; treat GUID comparisons here as case-insensitive. A workspace with no capacity assigned cannot host a mirror lakehouse.

EntityDescription.description: One table to include in the link, named together with the system it comes from.

Type.description: The table's logical name, as returned in LogicalName by the linkable-tables list (or IntersectLogicalName for an N:N intersect table).

EntitySource.description: Which system owns the table: Dataverse for a table from the linkable-tables list, FnO for one from the Finance and Operations table list.

LakehouseArtifactsCreateRequest.description: Create a Link to Fabric for an environment: provision a mirror lakehouse in the named Fabric workspace, bind it to the named Fabric-to-Dataverse connection, and start mirroring the named tables. This is the shape both portals send when establishing a link for the first time.

OrganizationId.description: The Dataverse organization id. Sent in the body as well as in the x-ms-organization-id header on the same request.

OrganizationUrl.description: The organization's instance URL. The service accepts it with or without a trailing slash.

EnvironmentFriendlyName.description: The environment's display name, from BAPI properties.linkedEnvironmentMetadata.friendlyName. It is used to name the Fabric lakehouse, so it is cosmetic to Dataverse but visible in Fabric.

EnvironmentUniqueName.description: The organization's unique name, from BAPI properties.linkedEnvironmentMetadata.uniqueName. Dataverse generates it as unq followed by the organization id with its hyphens stripped and truncated; it is not free text and must be passed through verbatim.

Entities.description: The logical names of the tables to mirror. Redundant with EntityDescriptions -- the same list in the same order -- but send both.

EntityDescriptions.description: The same tables as Entities, each tagged with its source system. This is the form that carries F&O tables, which Entities alone cannot express.

IsManagedLake.description: Whether athena provisions and owns the storage (true, the Link to Fabric case) rather than writing into a customer-supplied Azure Data Lake Storage account (false, the bring-your-own-lake Synapse case). True for a Link to Fabric.

WorkspaceId.description: The Fabric workspace to create the lakehouse in, from the Fabric Workspaces list. The workspace must be on a Fabric capacity.

ConnectionId.description: The Fabric-to-Dataverse connection the lakehouse will read through. It is created in Fabric, not here, and it authenticates **Fabric reading Dataverse**, not the reverse -- as the target workspace's system-assigned identity, which must already be a Dataverse application user holding the Synapse Link Service Access role.

LakehouseArtifactsResyncRequest.description: Resynchronise the Fabric-side shortcuts of an existing link after its table list has changed. Sent with removeShortcutsFirst=true against a lake that already exists, and identified by LakeId and FolderId rather than by a connection: it does not create a lakehouse and carries no table list, because the table list has already been changed through the lake profile.

LakeId.description: The datalakefolder id of the existing lake, from the Data Lakes list. Set it to the same value as FolderId.

FolderId.description: The datalakefolder id again; set it to the same value as LakeId.

WorkspaceId.description: The Fabric workspace holding the existing mirror lakehouse.

DatalakefolderUniqueName.description: The Dataverse datalakefolder row to resynchronise, by unique name. cds3_workspace is the Link to Fabric folder; cds2_workspace is the older Synapse Link folder. Note the lower-case f in the property name -- it does not match the DatalakeFolderUniqueName spelling used in the Data Lakes response.

LakehouseArtifacts.description: The Fabric artifacts now backing the environment's link, as a plain JSON object.

WorkspaceId.description: The Fabric workspace the lakehouse was created in; echoes the request.

LakehouseId.description: The Fabric lakehouse athena created. This is the only place the caller learns it from this operation, but it is also returned by the Data Lakes list afterwards.

ConnectionId.description: The Fabric-to-Dataverse connection the lakehouse reads through; echoes the request.

LakeDetail.description: One data lake destination attached to the environment. The shape is shared between the managed-Fabric case and the bring-your-own Azure Data Lake Storage case, so roughly half the fields are empty strings in either configuration rather than absent.

Id.description: The Dataverse datalakefolder id. **This is the id the rest of the surface is addressed by**: it is the datalakeFolderId for deleting lakehouse artifacts and the profileId for reading and updating the lake profile.

LakehouseId.description: The Fabric lakehouse that mirrors the data. Empty for a bring-your-own-lake link.

LakehouseWorkspaceId.description: The Fabric workspace containing that lakehouse.

TenantId.description: The tenant that owns the lake. For a managed lake this is the tenant of the storage athena provisioned, which is not necessarily the customer's tenant.

DatalakeFolderUniqueName.description: The datalakefolder row's unique name. cds3_workspace backs a Link to Fabric, cds2_workspace the older Synapse Link. Both rows exist on every organization whether or not it has ever been linked, so their presence in Dataverse means nothing -- presence in *this* list is what indicates a live link.

IsManaged.description: Whether athena owns the storage. True for Link to Fabric; false for a customer-supplied Azure Data Lake Storage account.

IsDefault.description: Whether this is the environment's default lake. False even on an environment with exactly one lake.

StorageAccountName.description: The Azure Storage account behind the lake. For a managed lake this is athena's own storage, named aeth followed by a hex string, and the caller has no access to it.

FileSystemName.description: The ADLS Gen2 filesystem (container) inside that storage account holding the mirrored data.

FileSystemEndpoint.description: The dfs.core.windows.net endpoint of the storage account. Populated even for a managed lake, where it is not usable by the caller.

SubscriptionId.description: The Azure subscription holding the storage account, for a bring-your-own-lake link. Empty string for a managed lake -- athena's own subscription is not disclosed.

ResourceGroupName.description: The resource group holding the storage account, for a bring-your-own-lake link. Empty string for a managed lake.

BlobEndpoint.description: Blob service endpoint of the storage account. Empty for a managed lake.

QueueEndpoint.description: Queue service endpoint of the storage account. Empty for a managed lake.

TableEndpoint.description: Table service endpoint of the storage account. Empty for a managed lake.

FileEndpoint.description: File service endpoint of the storage account. Empty for a managed lake.

WorkspaceDevEndpoint.description: The Azure Synapse workspace development endpoint, for a link that targets Synapse rather than Fabric. Empty for a Link to Fabric.

SynapseDatabaseName.description: The serverless SQL database created in that Synapse workspace. Empty for a Link to Fabric.

IsCDS2.description: Whether the row is the legacy cds2_workspace folder. It reads false on a cds3_workspace row; like IsCDS3 it is not worth branching on, since DatalakeFolderUniqueName carries the same distinction reliably.

IsCDS3.description: Whether the row is the cds3_workspace folder. **It reads false even on a row whose DatalakeFolderUniqueName is exactly cds3_workspace.** Do not branch on it; read DatalakeFolderUniqueName instead.

IsComplianceLake.description: Whether the lake is a compliance-scoped lake. False for an ordinary Link to Fabric.

IsDeltaLakeWriterEnabled.description: Whether the Delta Lake writer is enabled for this lake, producing Delta tables rather than CSV. False for a Link to Fabric.

DataProcessingConfigurationId.description: Id of the data processing configuration driving the sync jobs. Empty for a Link to Fabric.

DeltaLakeMaintenanceDPCId.description: Id of the data processing configuration that runs Delta Lake maintenance. Null when the lake has none.

AccessType.description: How the lake is accessed, as an enumeration value. 0 for a managed lake.

Path.description: Path prefix within the filesystem. Null for a managed lake.

RetryPolicy.description: How the sync engine retries a failed export batch for this profile.

MaxRetryCount.description: Attempts before the batch is abandoned. The service sets 12.

IntervalInSeconds.description: Delay between attempts. The service sets 5.

Backoff.description: Backoff strategy, as an enumeration value. The service sets 0.

ErrorDetails.description: The last error against a table's sync, all three fields empty strings when there has been none. This is the only error structure anywhere on this surface, and it is reported inside a 200 rather than raised as a status code.

Code.description: Error code. Empty while the table's sync has not failed; the service publishes no code vocabulary.

Message.description: Human-readable message. The lake profile read takes a publishErrorMessageToUI parameter that governs whether this is populated for display.

Details.description: Additional detail, typically a stack or inner exception.

LakeProfileEntityStatus.description: Per-table progress counters for the current initial-sync run, as the sync engine keeps them.

Type.description: The table's logical name; repeats the parent's Type.

ProfileId.description: The profile's own Id -- not the datalakefolder id the profile is addressed by.

TotalNotifications.description: Change notifications received for this table since the counters were last reset.

FailureNotifications.description: Notifications that failed to export. Non-zero here is the signal that a table is stuck; ErrorDetails on the parent says why.

LastExportDate.description: When data for this table was last written to the lake. The .NET DateTime zero value 0001-01-01T00:00:00 means never, rather than null.

LastExportStatus.description: Where the last export got to. PostProcessing means the rows are written and the lakehouse shortcut or table registration is still being created -- a table in PostProcessing is not yet queryable in Fabric.

EntityMetadataState.description: Whether the table's schema has been created in the destination. The string form of the parent's numeric MetadataState.

ExpectedInitialSyncNotifications.description: How many notifications the initial sync expects to process, which tracks the table's row count at the moment sync started. 0 for an empty table.

InitialSyncState.description: Progress of this table's initial full sync. Moves to Completed only after PostProcessing finishes.

VersionNumber.description: Dataverse change-tracking version the sync has consumed to. long.MinValue (-9223372036854775808) is the sentinel for "not yet established", and it is what this field carries even for tables whose initial sync has completed.

ChangeTime.description: Timestamp paired with VersionNumber; the .NET DateTime zero value means unset.

MetadataVersionNumber.description: As VersionNumber, for schema changes rather than data changes. Same long.MinValue sentinel.

LakeProfileEntity.description: One table inside a lake profile: how it is configured for mirroring, and how far its sync has got. Read-only fields far outnumber settable ones -- see the update operation for which six the service accepts back.

MetadataState.description: Numeric state of the destination schema for this table: 1 while it has not been created, 8 once it has. The same fact is available as the string EntityMetadataState under Status.

Settings.description: Per-table settings bag. The service returns an empty object and no keys are documented; send an empty object on update.

AppendOnlyMode.description: Whether updates and deletes are written to the lake as additional rows rather than modifying existing ones, preserving full change history at the cost of requiring the consumer to deduplicate. Settable on update.

PartitionStrategy.description: How the table's data is partitioned in the lake. Year produces fewer, larger partitions; Month suits high-volume tables. Settable on update.

RecordCountPerBlock.description: Rows written per block during export. The service stores 125, and replaces a 0 sent for a newly added table with 125. Settable on update.

SyncDataFromLastNDays.description: Limit the initial sync to rows changed within this many days. -1 means no limit -- mirror the whole table.

DeltaSyncJobTriggerIntervalMins.description: How often delta sync runs for this table, in minutes. -1 means the table follows the profile's own IncrementalUpdateTimeInterval instead of having its own schedule; a positive value, such as 20, gives it one.

GenerateParquet.description: Whether data is written as Parquet rather than CSV.

EnableEnumSupport.description: Whether option-set columns are materialised with their labels rather than as raw integers.

IsGUIDAndDateTimeOffsetSupported.description: Whether the destination schema uses native GUID and datetimeoffset types rather than strings. True for a Link to Fabric.

SyncState.description: Delta-sync state for this table. It reads NotStarted even for tables whose initial sync has completed, so it does not track delta sync progress; CurrentState does.

CurrentState.description: The single field to poll when waiting for a table to become queryable. It walks InitialSyncNotStarted, InitialSyncInProgress, InitialSyncPostProcessing, then InProgress -- which means initial sync is done and the table is on delta sync, not that anything is still running.

LastSynchronizedOn.description: When the table last had data written. Null before the first write.

AdditionTime.description: When the table was added to the profile.

InitialSyncMetadataCreatedTime.description: When the destination schema for the table was created.

InitialSyncDataCompletedTime.description: When the initial data load finished writing.

InitialSyncProcessCompleteTime.description: When post-processing after the initial load finished. Later than InitialSyncDataCompletedTime, and the point at which the table is actually usable.

LastDeltaSyncMetadataTime.description: When a schema change was last picked up by delta sync. Null until one is.

LastDeltaSyncDataTime.description: When data was last picked up by delta sync. Null until the first delta sync writes.

DestinationCount.description: Rows currently in the destination. Compare with CrmRecordCount to see whether the mirror is complete; null before the first count runs.

CrmRecordCount.description: Rows currently in the Dataverse table, as of LastCrmCountModifiedTime.

LastCrmCountModifiedTime.description: When CrmRecordCount was last recomputed. Note the format differs from every other timestamp in this payload: it carries sub-second precision and a Z suffix, where the others are unzoned to the second.

EntityPauseResumeOperationsType.description: Pause/resume state for this table, as an enumeration value. 0 for a table that has not been paused.

SynapseTableCreationState.description: Progress of creating the table in a Synapse serverless database. NotStarted for a Fabric link, which does not use Synapse.

IsDeltaSyncTriggerCreated.description: Whether the delta-sync trigger for this table has been created.

IsArchivalEnabled.description: Whether Dataverse long-term retention data for this table is included in the mirror.

LastHardDeleteTime.description: When hard-deleted rows were last reconciled out of the lake.

MinDataSyncVersion.description: Lowest change-tracking version retained for this table.

IsVarBinaryRedactSupportedForFnOTables.description: Finance and Operations capability flag: whether varbinary columns are redacted rather than mirrored. False for a Dataverse table.

IsGUIDSupportedForFnOTables.description: Finance and Operations capability flag: whether GUID columns use a native type.

IsValidDateEffectiveFieldsSupportedForFn.description: Finance and Operations capability flag: whether date-effective (valid-from/valid-to) columns are mirrored as such.

IsArrayFiledSupportedForFnOTables.description: Finance and Operations capability flag: whether array columns are mirrored. Spelled Filed, not Field, on the wire.

IsFnOTableDeltaSyncIntervalChanged.description: Finance and Operations flag: whether the table's delta sync interval has been overridden.

IsFnORecIdVersionIdxCreated.description: Finance and Operations flag: whether the RecId/Version index has been created in the destination.

IsEdtArrayEnumTypeFilterSupported.description: Finance and Operations flag: whether extended-data-type array and enum filters are supported.

LakeProfileEntityUpdate.description: One table as sent on an update. The read returns fifty-odd fields per table; the update sends these six, and everything else is either recomputed or preserved by the service.

Type.description: The table's logical name. A table present here and absent from the stored profile is added to the link; a table absent here and present in the stored profile is removed from it.

AppendOnlyMode.description: See the same field on the read shape.

PartitionStrategy.description: See the same field on the read shape.

RecordCountPerBlock.description: Rows per export block. Send 0 for a table being added and the service stores 125, so 0 reads as "use the default".

Settings.description: Per-table settings bag. Send an empty object.

LakeProfileStatus.description: Profile-wide sync status, aggregated across the tables in it.

ExportStatus.description: Outcome of the last export cycle. Success once a cycle has completed without error.

InitialSyncState.description: Whether the profile's initial sync has finished. It reads Completed while individual tables are still in InitialSyncInProgress, so it is not a reliable aggregate. Poll the per-table CurrentState instead.

LastExportDate.description: When the profile last exported. Null even where individual tables carry export dates; read those instead.

LastModifiedOn.description: When the profile was last changed. Equal to the profile's own LastModified.

MetadataState.description: Whether the destination schema has been created for the profile as a whole. Reads NotCreated while a newly added table's schema is still being built.

ForceRefreshState.description: Progress of a caller-requested full refresh. NotStarted -- no operation on this surface starts one.

LakeProfile.description: The synapselinkprofile for one data lake, with its full per-table sync state. This is the only place the progress of a Link to Fabric is observable.

Id.description: The synapselinkprofile's own id. **Not** the id this resource is addressed by -- the path takes the datalakefolder id, and these are different GUIDs.

State.description: Profile lifecycle state. 1 -- active -- from creation until the profile is deleted.

LastModified.description: When the profile was last changed.

Name.description: The profile's name, generated by the service as CDS3_ followed by the organization id. Not free text.

DestinationType.description: Where the profile writes. 4 is the managed Fabric lakehouse; Synapse and a customer-owned ADLS account have their own values.

DestinationKeyVaultUri.description: Key Vault holding the destination credential, for destinations that need one. The literal string "dummy" for a managed Fabric lakehouse, which needs no stored credential -- the service does not use null here.

DestinationPrefix.description: Prefix applied to destination table names. Empty when the tables take their own names.

DestinationSchemaName.description: Schema the destination tables are created in. dbo.

LakeId.description: The datalakefolder id this profile writes to -- the same value as the path id.

WriteDeleteLog.description: Whether deletes are written to a delete log in the lake so consumers can reconcile them. True for a Link to Fabric.

CountFeature.description: Whether row-count reconciliation between Dataverse and the lake is enabled. False for a Link to Fabric, which is why DestinationCount and CrmRecordCount move only during initial sync.

CreationTime.description: When the profile was created -- which is when lakehouse artifacts were created, since the caller never creates a profile directly.

ActivationTime.description: When the profile was last activated. Set on creation and moved forward by each activate call.

UpdateTime.description: When the profile was last updated. Null until the first update.

NeedCopyAttachmentsToBlob.description: Whether attachment binaries are copied into blob storage alongside the row data rather than left in Dataverse.

NeedCopyFileTypeAttachmentsToBlob.description: As NeedCopyAttachmentsToBlob, for file-type columns specifically.

EnabledForJobs.description: Whether the sync jobs run at all. **This is the profile's on switch**: false stops mirroring without deleting anything. True on a live link.

EnabledForIncrementalUpdate.description: Whether incremental-update folders are produced in addition to the mirrored tables, giving consumers a change feed on the IncrementalUpdateTimeInterval cadence.

IncrementalUpdateTimeInterval.description: Cadence of incremental update in minutes. Settable on update; 15 and 60 are both accepted.

EnabledForDeltaLake.description: Whether output is written in Delta Lake format rather than CSV.

EnabledForDlw.description: Whether the Data Lake Writer pipeline is used. True for a Link to Fabric.

SynapseSyncState.description: Progress of Synapse serverless database creation. NotStarted for a Fabric link.

LinkedToFabric.description: Whether the profile targets a Fabric lakehouse rather than Synapse or a raw ADLS account. True for a Link to Fabric.

EnabledForFnOTablesBaseEnumSupport.description: Whether Finance and Operations base enumerations are materialised with labels.

IsDeDuplicationJobsSubmitted.description: Whether deduplication jobs have been queued for this profile, which append-only output eventually needs.

LinkedFnOEnvironmentLastObservedValue.description: The linked Finance and Operations environment as last seen. Null when there is none.

ShouldSkipShortCutsDeletionInOLCFlow.description: Whether the Fabric shortcuts are left in place during an organization lifecycle (OLC) operation such as a copy or restore, instead of being deleted and rebuilt.

ProfilePauseResumeOperationsType.description: Pause/resume state for the profile, as an enumeration value. 0 for a profile that has not been paused.

LinkedFnOEnvironmentCurrentAOSCount.description: Application Object Server instance count of the linked Finance and Operations environment. 0 when there is none.

LinkedFnOEnvironmentAdditionalAOSCount.description: Additional AOS instances provisioned for the linked Finance and Operations environment.

Entities.description: The tables in the link, each with its configuration and sync state.

LakeProfileUpdate.description: A whole lake profile as sent on an update. Read the profile, replace Entities and any settings being changed, drop the server-computed per-table fields, and send everything else back unmodified -- so this is the read shape with nothing removed except the depth of Entities.

LinkedFnOEnvironmentCurrentAOSCount.description: Application Object Server instance count of the linked Finance and Operations environment. 0 when there is none.

LinkedFnOEnvironmentAdditionalAOSCount.description: Additional AOS instances provisioned for the linked Finance and Operations environment.

Entities.description: The complete desired table list. It replaces the stored list rather than merging into it: omitting a table removes it from the link.

LakeProfileState.description: The profile's identity and lifecycle state, returned in place of the full profile by operations that change it.

Id.description: The profile's own id, not the datalakefolder id.

EnterprisePolicyClientCredentials.description: The client credential the environment's encryption enterprise policy makes available to the sync engine, for a customer-managed-key environment. Both fields are null when the environment has no such policy.

ClientSecretUrl.description: Key Vault secret URI holding the client secret. Null when no enterprise policy applies.

ClientId.description: Application id to authenticate as. Null when no enterprise policy applies.
